title: Frontend: Prim's MST Algorithm
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Prim's MST Algorithm. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}) for a weighted undirected connected graph, vertices 0..count-1 and edges [a,b,weight]. Return total MST weight using dense Prim selection; count=0 returns 0. Disconnected graphs throw Disconnected. Negative and parallel edges are supported.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Grow a visited set from one start vertex.
alternativeApproaches: Return a minimum spanning forest for disconnected input and explain why directed graphs need a different problem formulation.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Single vertex; equal weights; negative weight.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
